title: Slice and search
intro: `substring(begin, end)` cuts in the gaps between characters: it includes `begin` and stops just before `end`. `indexOf` returns where something first appears, or `-1`. And every method that seems to change a String returns a new one.

rounds.right: `substring` cuts at two gaps: `begin` is the first index you keep, `end` the first you don't. Leave `end` out and it runs to the end.

why.begin: `{expr}` starts at index {b}: count from 0 at the first character.
why.end: Nearly: `{expr}` stops before index {e}, so that box is left out. The last character you get is at index {lastIn}.
why.span: `{expr}` returns the characters from index {b} up to, but not including, index {e}: the last one is at index {lastIn}.
why.call: `{chosen}` returns {got}. The end index is left out, so it must be one past the last character you want.

rounds.right: `indexOf` searches from index 0 and stops at the first match; when nothing matches, it returns `-1`, an index no character can have.

why.later: There is a {ch} there, but `indexOf` searches from index 0 and stops at the first one it meets.
why.absent: There is no {ch} in `{name}`, so no box can be the answer.
why.missing: `-1` means not found, but there is a {ch} in `{name}`: click the first box that holds one.

rounds.prompt: Each call returns a new String. What does it return?
rounds.right: `trim` drops the whitespace at the two ends only, and `replace` swaps every match. Neither touched the original: each returned a new String.

why.trim.all: `trim()` only removes whitespace at the two ends. The space between the words is part of the text, so it stays.
why.trim.front: `trim()` works on both ends, not just the start.
why.trim.same: `trim()` returns a new String without the outer spaces. The String in `{a}` never changes, but this asks what the call returns.
why.replace.first: `replace` swaps every match, not just the first one.
why.replace.same: `replace` returns a new String with every `'e'` swapped. The String in `{a}` never changes, but the call's result is new.

rounds.prompt: `split` cuts a String at every separator and returns the pieces as a `String[]`.
rounds.right: `split` returned an array of the pieces between the separators, and array indexes count from 0 too.

why.split.commas: `split` cuts at every `;`: count the pieces between them, not the separators.
why.split.plus: `split` makes one piece for each stretch of text between separators: there is no extra empty piece here.
why.split.before: `[1]` is the second piece: array indexes count from 0.
why.split.after: `[1]` is the second piece, counting from 0: `[0]` is the first.
